cells.tense: The room is in front of you now, and you are reading it well.
cells.act: keep the ritual and give it room to change
cells.ask: Take the practice your people keep together that means the most to you. Hold it whole, and change one piece of it — a piece you chose, not an accident. No deadline on when you do.
cells.core:
You can stand in a room full of differing wants and hold the whole thing without dropping yourself. When someone shifts, you shift with them. When a moment needs something named, you name it. That give in you is not a lack of a position. It is the position, and you stay in it, which is how you can move.

What you have been taking in is asking to be handed on. Take the practice your people keep together that means the most to you, hold it as it is, and change one piece of it — a piece you chose. Keep it whole while you change it, so it stays the same practice for the others. A shared thing does not die because someone adapts it. It dies when nobody will hold it while it grows, and holding it is what you are doing now.
cells.sheetLine: You hold several sides of a room without losing your own.
cells.verb: sensing what a moment needs and adjusting to it without losing your own line
cells.place: the threshold where what you've absorbed with others becomes something you can carry out of the room

cells.tense: You are smoothing the room before it can show you anything.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Name a want you have been keeping quiet so the room stays easy. Take the first step on it today, before smoothing can begin, in whatever form the step actually takes.
cells.core:
Where you practise this, the room does not get to have an edge. Your read on how people are doing arrives before anyone has spoken, and by then you have already adjusted, already rounded the corner off, already decided which version of events will keep the peace. The skill is real. It is running ahead of what is actually being said, and the differences that need to be drawn are the ones you are drawing away.

There is a want in your life being kept small so it will not disturb anybody. It does not need to be announced. Take the first step on it today, before the smoothing can start. Direction from a real want steadies you faster than another adjustment does, and you are easier to be around when you are not the only one holding everything up.

cells.tense: You have left every step you took unattended, and the steps are what would have held.
cells.act: feel it alongside them and keep your own side
cells.ask: Think of someone you saw carrying something heavy. Sit with how it lands in you for as long as it takes, fix nothing, take nothing on, then go back to your own day.
cells.core:
Where this sits in you, nothing gathers. You move through a room, pick up pieces of other people's strain, and set each one down somewhere different on the way out, so nothing stacks into a whole you could point to. It is not that you do not care. It is that each contact scatters you a little further than the last, and you come out with nothing of your own that stayed in place.

A step is available that is not effort. Think of someone you saw carrying something heavy. Sit with how it lands in you, fix nothing, take nothing on, then return to your day. On your own time, with nobody told. What you are practising is being close to something without moving into it, and that is what starts to gather you back around your own center.

cells.tense: You have been combining things in a way you would not recognise if it were written down.
cells.act: learn how the people before you did it
cells.ask: Choose something the people you came up with used to do — a dish, a phrase, a way of marking a day. Ask someone older how it was really done, or look it up, and learn one version with your own hands.
cells.core:
The pieces you have taken in from a hundred different places are already fitting together. You carry a way of handling people, a sense of what a moment needs, and it feels like just how you are. You have been doing the joining without putting your name on it, with your attention elsewhere. Seeing it or not does not change that it happens.

Go back to where the joining came from before you. There is a way the people before you did something — said a thing, marked a day, cooked a dish — and you learned it by watching, which counts as learning it. Learn one of those properly: ask someone older how it was really done, or look it up. A practice people kept long enough to hand down has a shape inside it. What you are holding is not only yours, and knowing the shape is yours to do.
